observation.visible_scene: A fixed top-down (flat-lay) shot of a table covered with a white surface. Small colored sticks/matchsticks are arranged to spell two lines of text, "DAY OF" on top and "THE GIRL" below, using pink, orange and teal sticks, with a continuous white wire-like path weaving around and between the letters like a circuit. Surrounding the text are decorative stick-built objects: a rocket on the left, a conical flask on the right, a large wrench along the bottom edge, plus scattered loose colored matches, a small calculator, a pair of tweezers, confetti and other craft items. The overall layout is identical from the first to the last frame.
visible_changes: The scene is held essentially static throughout the excerpt: no object is added, removed, translated, or rotated across the frame, and the camera shows no pan, tilt, zoom or rotation (background edges and all peripheral objects stay in the same pixel positions).

The only frame-to-frame differences are tiny positional wobbles of individual sticks and of the white wire segments (e.g. the pink vertical strokes of the 'H' in 'THE' and the horizontal bars of the 'E' in 'THE' flicker slightly in length/presence), consistent with stop-motion/compression jitter rather than a directional build or motion.
Colors, letter shapes and the routing of the white wire path remain persistent across all sampled frames.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether this held composition is part of a longer stop-motion build-up or circuit animation that begins before or continues after the cropped segment (both crop ends are arbitrary and show the same finished-looking layout).
Any intended 'lighting' or 'flowing current' effect that the white wire path might suggest, since no illumination change is visible within the excerpt.
uncertain_details: The slight appearance/disappearance of a few stick segments (notably on the 'H' and 'E' of 'THE') could be either genuine micro stop-motion adjustments or rendering/compression noise; the excerpt is too short and too subtle to confirm a deliberate add/remove action.
No editing cut is visible inside the segment, so all observed variation is treated as continuous-frame jitter rather than a transition between two shots.
